scan.summary: This is an Oregon air contaminant discharge permit issued by the Department of Environmental Quality authorizing Cascade Specialty Chemicals to operate chemical storage and repackaging equipment with vapor control at its Portland facility. The permit specifies operating conditions for two scrubbers and solvent storage tanks, with requirements for daily monitoring, quarterly maintenance, monthly carbon replacement, and annual reporting. The permit expires November 15, 2026.
scan.freshness_note: This permit was issued September 1, 2021 and expires November 15, 2026. As of today (September 25, 2026), the permit is within 52 days of expiration. A renewal application must be submitted by July 18, 2026 to maintain continuous operation. The company should have already filed or be filing urgently if not yet submitted.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in all permit details as read from the document. The permit itself is issued by Oregon DEQ and sets conditions that are the agency's responsibility to enforce, not deficiencies in the company's document. Critical concern: the renewal deadline of July 18, 2026 has passed as of today (September 25, 2026). I cannot determine from the permit whether the company submitted a timely renewal application. If no renewal application was filed by July 18, 2026, the permit lapsed on November 15, 2026, and the company is operating without legal authorization as of today. This is urgent and should be verified immediately with Oregon DEQ. The permit provides clear, specific conditions with measurable parameters (pressure drop ranges, opacity limits, inspection frequency, reporting deadlines). The conditions are enforceable and well-documented.
